items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are clear (worker_loop, stop_workers, first_exception, worker_tasks) and there is a docstring. Small nits: the redundant `int(min(...))` and the needless `res = task_fn(); await res`. The shield/fallback gather has no comment, but the docstring covers the intent.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The agent left scratch/test_run.py, test_sigint.py and test_suite.py in /app. Each contains a copy-pasted run_tasks and print debug output. It also hand-rolls a queue, flags and cancellation where a Semaphore with TaskGroup would do, so the code is longer than needed.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Rejects max_concurrent<=0. The two `except BaseException` blocks always re-raise, so nothing is swallowed. Workers are cancelled and awaited under shield, with a fallback gather if cancelled again. Nothing is left orphaned. No magic constants.

items.name: Failures and degenerate arguments
items.evidence: Empty list returns early, and `raise ValueError("max_concurrent must be greater than 0")` handles bad limits. On failure, `stop_workers=True` stops queued tasks from starting, running workers are cancelled and gathered, and `raise first_exception` passes the original error up.

items.name: Required signature and import behaviour
items.name_zh: 签名与导入行为符合要求
items.evidence: `async def run_tasks(tasks: list[Callable[[], Awaitable[None]]], max_concurrent: int) -> None` in /app/run.py. Each callable is invoked only when a worker picks it up. Stdlib only, nothing runs at import, and all hidden tests passed.
